$schema_note: The tool catalog for the bitcoineconomy.ai marketplace: equipment an autonomous agent installs or runs to transact in Bitcoin — wallets & treasuries, node toolkits, ecash software, bridges & swaps, and the protocol primitives (L402, NWC, BOLT12, LNURL, MCP). Distinct from the service registry at /directory.json (what an agent BUYS); this is what it EQUIPS. Each tool: toolbox_group, tool_type, layer (where it sits in the stack), prereq_tier (what must be in place first), maintainer, repo/docs/site links, and mcp_endpoint where the tool ships its own MCP server (connect there to act). Full per-tool detail (gotchas, dependencies, verified specs) at card_url. Reference facts, not endorsements. Queryable via the /mcp server: find_tool, get_tool, list_mcp_servers.
name: The Marketplace tool catalog — bitcoineconomy.ai

prereq_tiers.keys-only: A keypair is enough — no node, no wallet, no funds
prereq_tiers.account: A hosted account (no identity check, but a human signs up first)
prereq_tiers.lightning-node: A funded Lightning node with channels (e.g. LND/CLN)
prereq_tiers.l2-network: Access to an L2/L3 network (Liquid, Spark, a federation)

tools.name: bitcoin-core
tools.tagline: The reference Bitcoin full node — the L1 root every self-custodial Lightning setup sits on. Validate the chain yourself, hold your own keys, and expose RPC for the tools above it.

tools.name: L402
tools.tagline: The HTTP-native payment protocol — pay a Lightning invoice to unlock an API, with a reusable credential proving you paid.

tools.name: Alby & Nostr Wallet Connect (NWC)
tools.tagline: A standard for controlling a Lightning wallet remotely — scoped, budgeted, and revocable — without ever handing over the keys.

mcp_endpoint.note: The payment MCP that complements the directory's discovery MCP — wraps a scoped, budgeted NWC (NIP-47) connection string as Lightning payment tools for an MCP-capable agent; the keys stay in the wallet. Honest status: the repo is archived (last commit 2025-06-20) and declares no license, but the @getalby/nwc-mcp-server npm package still installs and runs (stdio by default; optional HTTP mode). Verify currency before relying on it in production.

tools.name: BOLT12 (Offers)
tools.tagline: Reusable Lightning payment requests — publish one "offer" and accept repeated payments against it, with receiver privacy via blinded paths.

tools.name: LNURL
tools.tagline: A family of small Lightning protocols (pay, withdraw, auth) and the Lightning Address — the pre-BOLT12 way to make payment endpoints discoverable over HTTPS.

tools.name: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
tools.tagline: The open standard for giving agents structured access to tools and data — the rail a Lightning payment server plugs into so an agent can pay from inside its workflow.

tools.name: Nostr
tools.tagline: The open identity-and-discovery layer under the agent stack — cryptographic keypairs for portable identity, and relays for censorship-resistant service discovery. It's how an agent finds providers and controls a wallet; the money itself rides Lightning/Cashu.

tools.name: CLINK (+ Lightning.Pub)
tools.tagline: ShockNet's open standards for Lightning payments over Nostr — static offers, direct debits, and delegated spending permissions, addressed to NIP-05 identities, no web server required.

tools.name: Cashu
tools.tagline: Chaumian bearer ecash on Bitcoin — instant, private, lightweight tokens an agent can hold and spend without channels or accounts.

tools.name: Fedimint
tools.tagline: Federated Bitcoin custody plus Chaumian ecash — a guardian federation holds the coins under threshold security while issuing private, Lightning-interoperable tokens.

tools.name: Evaluating an ecash mint
tools.tagline: How to judge whether a Cashu or Fedimint mint is trustworthy — the hard solvency signals, the reputation layer, and the one rule that beats all of them.

tools.name: Spark
tools.tagline: A shared-UTXO, Lightning-compatible Bitcoin L2 for instant, near-zero-cost transfers of BTC and Bitcoin-native assets — no bridges, no wrapping.

tools.name: lightning-agent-tools
tools.tagline: Lightning Labs' production AI-agent toolkit — composable skills plus an MCP server that let an agent run a node, pay L402 APIs, host paid endpoints, and keep its keys isolated.

tools.name: LNbits
tools.tagline: The most widely deployed programmable Lightning platform — isolated wallets, a clean REST API, and an extension ecosystem on top of any node backend.

tools.name: Minibits Ippon
tools.tagline: A Cashu wallet built from the ground up for AI agents — create and fund a short-lived, single-purpose wallet in one HTTP call or CLI command.

tools.name: Xverse Agent Wallet
tools.tagline: A self-custodial Bitcoin wallet built for AI agents — it answers an HTTP 402 by paying the Lightning invoice itself, no human checkout.

tools.name: BitAgent
tools.tagline: An early, open-source framework for agent-to-agent commerce — agents discover each other over Nostr, verify identity with DIDs, and settle work in sats over Lightning.

tools.name: Agentic AQUA
tools.tagline: Jan3's open-source MCP wallet — an AI assistant generates addresses, checks balances, and sends Bitcoin, Liquid, or Lightning (via Boltz swaps) from one seed, by natural language.

tools.name: Boltz
tools.tagline: Non-custodial atomic swaps between on-chain Bitcoin, Lightning, and Liquid — the submarine-swap bridge, exposed as an API.

tools.name: Loop
tools.tagline: Lightning Labs' non-custodial liquidity bridge — Loop Out and Loop In move balance between Lightning and on-chain via submarine swaps.

tools.name: Amboss
tools.tagline: A Lightning channel-liquidity marketplace — buy inbound capacity from a public market with one API call (or an MIT MCP server), no account needed.

mcp_endpoint.note: Amboss's own MCP server — connect here to actually buy inbound liquidity. One stdio tool; needs your node connection_uri and an LND/CLN/Eclair wallet to pay the HODL invoice.

tools.name: Taproot Assets
tools.tagline: Lightning Labs' protocol for issuing assets — including stablecoins — on Bitcoin and moving them over Lightning rails. Lightning rails for assets, not Bitcoin substrate.
